rationale: Daily bowel movements decreased during treatment for thyroid cancer-associated secretory diarrhea. Parkinson constipation was not observed and no stool counts or comparable culinary dose are available.
Interviews describe nutmeg use for diarrhea. Route and preparation are pooled in the table, and constipation is reported for a different plant.

The one-group report gives 12 constipated before carrot juice and 3 after. The paper does not report usable preparation, intake duration, concurrent comparator or paired transitions, and pregnancy-specific determinants limit transfer to Parkinson constipation after steamed carrot.
The reprint asserts insomnia benefit without case observations. A second dated annual repeats the same attribution, which supplies no independent family.
The original abstract identifies insomnia as a customary use. The preparation, exposure-outcome comparison and methods separate from the abstract remain open.
